boards.title: Your First Weekend at Milwaukee School of Engineering, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-pressure, under-21-safe sequence of campus and downtown Milwaukee stops for a first weekend.

cards.title: Start at the Campus Center
cards.subtitle: 1025 N. Broadway
cards.notes: Use the Campus Center as a practical first stop: orient yourself, find student services, then pause in the social spaces before heading out.
cards.short_summary: A central on-campus starting point with services, dining, games and gathering space.
cards.evidence_claim: MSOE identifies the Campus Center as a social hub with student services, games, pool and the Robert Spitzer Dining Commons.
cards.access_notes: Campus building; check current building access before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Dwight and Dian Diercks Computational Science Hall
cards.title: See the Diercks Hall atrium
cards.subtitle: 1025 N. Milwaukee St.
cards.notes: Walk to Diercks Hall and look through the first-floor atrium, where the video wall and plaza-facing doors make the building easy to recognize.
cards.short_summary: A campus technology building with a first-floor collaboration atrium.
cards.evidence_claim: MSOE says Diercks Hall's first-floor atrium supports group collaboration and events and includes a sixteen-screen video wall.
cards.access_notes: Building access may vary; view public areas only when open.

cards.entity_name: Patricia E. Kern Conservatory of Music
cards.title: Find the music conservatory
cards.subtitle: 308 E. Juneau Ave.
cards.notes: Make a short campus walk to the conservatory and note its location for future rehearsals, ensemble events or a quieter creative detour.
cards.short_summary: MSOE's home for music programs and student ensembles.
cards.evidence_claim: MSOE identifies the Patricia E. Kern Conservatory of Music as the home of its music programs and ensembles.
cards.access_notes: Confirm event and building access with MSOE before entering.

cards.title: Get moving at the Kern Center
cards.subtitle: 1245 N. Broadway
cards.notes: Bring your campus ID, check availability, and use the recreation spaces that fit your plans, such as the track, field house or fitness areas.
cards.evidence_claim: MSOE lists the Kern Center's ice arena, basketball arena, fitness center, field house, running track and wrestling area.
cards.access_notes: Academic-year hours list Saturday 8 a.m.–8 p.m. and Sunday 10 a.m.–8 p.m.; MSOE says availability can change and student swipe access applies.

cards.title: Check out Viets Field
cards.subtitle: MSOE athletic facilities
cards.notes: Take a lap around the outdoor field area or watch for a scheduled activity, while giving teams and reserved events their space.
cards.short_summary: An MSOE outdoor recreation and athletic facility.
cards.evidence_claim: MSOE lists Viets Field among its athletics and recreation facilities and publishes academic-year operating hours.
cards.access_notes: Academic-year hours list 6:30 a.m.–8 p.m. Friday through Sunday; check the 25live calendar because weather and events can affect access.

cards.title: Visit the Grohmann Museum
cards.subtitle: 1000 N. Broadway
cards.notes: Set aside time for the collection and building, then check the museum's exhibition calendar before you go so your visit matches current gallery access.
cards.short_summary: An MSOE museum devoted to art depicting human work.
cards.evidence_claim: The Grohmann Museum lists gallery hours and presents exhibitions and events on MSOE's campus.
cards.access_notes: Listed gallery hours are Monday–Friday 9 a.m.–5 p.m., Saturday noon–6 p.m., and Sunday 1–4 p.m. Admission is listed separately.

cards.title: Locate Walter Schroeder Library
cards.subtitle: MSOE campus
cards.notes: Find the library early and save it as a reliable reference point for coursework; ask staff about visitor policies and study-space access when you arrive.
cards.evidence_claim: MSOE includes Walter Schroeder Library among the buildings on its campus.
cards.access_notes: Confirm current entry, borrowing and study-space policies directly with the library.

cards.title: Take a RiverWalk reset
cards.subtitle: Downtown Milwaukee riverfront
cards.notes: Choose a daylight stretch of the public RiverWalk for a calm walk between downtown stops, using marked access points and staying on the designated path.
cards.short_summary: A public pedestrian route along the Milwaukee River.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Milwaukee says the RiverWalk is open to the public 24 hours a day, 365 days a year, free of charge.
cards.source_title: Welcome to Milwaukee's Riverwalk | City of Milwaukee
cards.access_notes: The City states it is publicly open 24 hours a day, 365 days a year; use normal pedestrian awareness after dark.

cards.title: Browse Milwaukee Public Market
cards.subtitle: 400 N. Water St.
cards.notes: Browse the independent merchants, then decide whether to buy a meal or simply use the visit to learn the downtown food options for another day.
cards.short_summary: An all-ages downtown market with independent food and retail merchants.
cards.evidence_claim: Milwaukee Public Market identifies itself as an all-ages gathering place at 400 N. Water Street with independent merchants and prepared foods.
cards.access_notes: Listed hours are Monday–Saturday 10 a.m.–8 p.m. and Sunday 10 a.m.–6 p.m.; purchases are optional but offered by merchants.

cards.title: End with Jazz in the Park
cards.subtitle: Cathedral Square Park, 520 E. Wells St.
cards.notes: If your first weekend falls during the summer series, bring a friend to Cathedral Square Park and check the official schedule before making the trip.
cards.short_summary: A recurring outdoor downtown music series at Cathedral Square Park.
cards.evidence_claim: Milwaukee County's 2026 events listing places Jazz in the Park at Cathedral Square Park on Thursdays from June 4 through September 24.
cards.access_notes: The current city listing gives Thursday live-music times of 6–9 p.m.; confirm weather and schedule details before attending.
